pages.title: Home
pages.seoTitle: Pahal Nepal Foundation: school meals and libraries in Sindhupalchok
pages.seoDescription: A Kathmandu nonprofit serving daily school meals and running libraries in Sindhupalchok and Dolakha since 2073. Audited accounts published every year.

props.title: A hot meal at ten, so the afternoon class is not lost
props.text: We pay local cooks to serve dal-bhat at eleven government schools in the hills above Melamchi, and we run a library room in each one.

image.alt: A person looking towards snow peaks

props.heading: Why meals, why there
props.body:
In the schools we work with, children walk one to two hours each way. Many arrive without eating and leave by two to reach home before dark. A meal at ten keeps them in the classroom until the last bell.

We buy rice, lentils and vegetables from farmers within the same ward, so the meal also pays a neighbour.

items.title: Daily school meals
items.text: A cook hired from the ward, a menu that changes with the season, and parents on a rota to help.

items.title: Library rooms
items.text: A shelf of Nepali storybooks, low tables and a trained volunteer teacher, in each school.

items.title: Teacher training
items.text: Two-day sessions in Melamchi Bazaar on reading in the early grades.

items.title: Started with one school in Helambu
items.text: Two cooks and 41 children, after the 2072 earthquake.

items.title: First library room
items.text: Opened in Melamchi, with books donated by a Patan school.

items.title: Eleven schools
items.text: Meals in all, libraries in nine.

props.title: Rs 28 feeds one child for one school day
props.text: Rs 5,000 feeds a class of thirty for six days.

pages.title: Where the money goes
pages.seoTitle: Where the money goes: Pahal Nepal Foundation accounts
pages.seoDescription: How Pahal Nepal Foundation spends donations: food, cooks, books and office costs. Audited accounts published every Ashwin.

props.heading: Where each rupee goes
props.body:
Last year, of every Rs 100 donated: Rs 71 went to food and cooks' pay, Rs 14 to library books and teacher training, Rs 9 to transport to the schools, and Rs 6 to the Kathmandu office.

These numbers come from our audited accounts, which are signed by an auditor registered with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal.

pages.title: Give or volunteer
pages.seoTitle: Give, volunteer or partner with Pahal Nepal Foundation
pages.seoDescription: Donate to school meals in Sindhupalchok, volunteer as a library teacher, or ask us to visit your school or company.

props.heading: Ways to help
props.body:
Give

eSewa and Fonepay to the Pahal QR, or a bank transfer to Pahal Nepal Foundation, Nabil Bank, Baluwatar branch. You get a receipt, and it is tax-deductible in Nepal.

Volunteer

Library teachers spend two weeks in a school in Helambu. Food and a bed at the school are provided.

Bring us to your company

We visit offices in Kathmandu to talk about workplace giving.

props.heading: Write to us
props.text: Tell us if you would like to give, volunteer, or invite us to talk. Anyone on the team can answer you.
props.success: Thank you. Someone from the team will reply within three working days.

props.heading: One letter after each term
props.text: What we served, what we read, and what it cost. Nothing else.
props.success: Thank you. You are on the list.
